event.title: Senate Approves Bipartisan Sanctions Bill Targeting Russia and Iran
event.canonical_title: Senate Approves Bipartisan Sanctions Bill Targeting Russia and Iran
event.summary: The Senate has passed a bipartisan bill imposing stricter sanctions on Russia and extending existing sanctions on Iran. The legislation, which received an overwhelming vote of 86-11, was championed by the late Senator Lindsey Graham, whose recent death expedited its passage. The bill aims to penalize countries that continue to purchase Russian oil and gas, aiming to reduce revenue for Russia amid ongoing conflicts.

timeline.title: US Senate Approves Comprehensive Sanctions Bill Against Russian Energy Sector
timeline.summary: The US Senate has approved a comprehensive sanctions package aimed at targeting Russia's energy revenues. The legislation includes sanctions on Russian officials, oligarchs, and financial institutions, as well as measures against the shadow fleet used to circumvent restrictions on oil exports. Additionally, it grants the President the authority to impose tariffs of up to 500% on Russian imports, including gas and oil.
key_facts: Sanctions target Russian energy revenues and officials.
Includes measures against financial institutions and shadow fleet.
President can impose tariffs up to 500% on Russian imports.

event_overview.title: About Russia Sanctions
event_overview.subject: Russia Sanctions
event_overview.summary: This event concerns the U.S. Senate’s August 7, 2026 passage of bipartisan legislation aimed at increasing economic pressure on Russia and on major foreign purchasers of Russian oil and gas, in the context of Russia’s war against Ukraine. The package also continued U.S. statutory sanctions authority affecting Iran’s energy and weapons sectors; Senate passage did not by itself make the measure law, which would also require House approval and presidential action.

facts.label: Senate action
facts.value: The Senate passed the Russia- and Iran-related sanctions package on August 7, 2026, by an 86–11 vote.

facts.label: Legislative origins
facts.value: The underlying Sanctioning Russia Act was introduced in the Senate as S. 1241 on April 1, 2025, with broad bipartisan sponsorship; the 2026 package followed negotiations to revise and advance Russia sanctions legislation.

facts.label: Russia-related scope
facts.value: The legislation is designed to authorize or require primary and secondary measures against Russian government-linked actors and those supporting Russia’s war, including Russian financial institutions, energy-related entities, the so-called shadow fleet, and specified foreign purchasers or enablers of Russian oil and gas.

facts.label: Foreign purchasers and tariffs
facts.value: The negotiated version allows targeted tariffs on imports from countries identified as among the largest buyers of Russian crude oil or gas, or among the leading countries facilitating evasion of Russia energy sanctions.

facts.label: Iran-related provision
facts.value: The package includes a provision intended to prevent the expiration of sanctions authority restricting financing for Iran’s energy and weapons sectors, alongside the Russia-focused measures.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline covers the Senate’s August 7, 2026 approval and its Russia- and Iran-related provisions, not subsequent House consideration, enactment, executive implementation, or later sanctions designations.
